# Default — Style Reference

> Smoked glass over a darkened control room, one green status lamp lit. Weight 400 Inter dims word by word on #0b0c0e, hairline light-rings stand in for borders, and green appears only when a workflow step has succeeded.

**Theme:** dark

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

Default speaks a graphite-console product language: a near-black canvas of #0b0c0e carries a four-step tonal stack (#0e0f11 for product stages, #121214 for cards, #151618 for raised wells, #171717 for filled controls) in which no two adjacent layers differ by more than about three RGB points. The chromatic budget is exactly one hue. Green (#22c55e as text, 27 uses, and #4ade80 as fill, 14 uses) is permitted only as product status: Qualified badges, Live dots, credit counters and "Run complete" ticks inside the simulated workflow. The marketing chrome itself stays grayscale. Typography is a single variable Inter. Display sizes of 52px and 64px are set at weight 400 with -0.02em tracking, and hierarchy is carried by white opacity rather than weight, as headlines fade from #ffffff to #ffffff80 mid-sentence. Shapes run from 4px to 16px with pills reserved for chips and avatars. Elevation comes from 0.5px to 1px light-rings, not drop shadows. The page reads as an instrument panel at rest rather than a marketing page shouting.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Jet Canvas | `#0b0c0e` | `--color-jet-canvas` | Body background, footer field and the inset ring inside icon wells — a blue-leaning near-black that keeps every lifted surface reading as glass rather than gray. |
| Onyx Well | `#0e0f11` | `--color-onyx-well` | Hero product stage, solution tiles and section bands (10 uses) — one step above canvas, enough to frame a mockup without drawing a border. |
| Carbon Card | `#121214` | `--color-carbon-card` | Bento feature cards, testimonial cards and mega-menu feature cards — the workhorse container surface, measured directly on 330×311px cards. |
| Graphite Raise | `#151618` | `--color-graphite-raise` | Circular icon wells, popover menus and arrow buttons (22 uses) — the highest resting surface, always paired with a light-ring. |
| Iron Fill | `#171717` | `--color-iron-fill` | Filled button backgrounds and form-field fills in mockups (15 uses) — a neutral, not blue-shifted, fill that separates controls from containers. |
| Paper | `#ffffff` | `--color-paper` | Lead words of display headlines, the announcement pill fill and icon glyphs (94 uses) — full white is the emphasis tier. Do not use it for body copy. |
| Paper Ink | `#ffffffe5` | `--color-paper-ink` | Body text, nav labels, card titles and the logo wordmark (119 uses, the most-used color) — 90% white softens glare on the dark canvas. |
| Fog Caption | `#ffffff80` | `--color-fog-caption` | Dimmed headline words, card eyebrows, testimonial roles and logo marquee (50 uses) — the second voice that carries hierarchy where other sites use weight. |
| Steel Border | `#2d2d2f` | `--color-steel-border` | Button outlines, chip borders and card dividers (29 uses) — the strongest neutral line, reserved for interactive edges. |
| Iron Hairline | `#1f1f21` | `--color-iron-hairline` | Footer top rule, section dividers and the outer icon-well ring (11 uses) — a structural line that is felt more than seen. |
| Signal Green | `#22c55e` | `--color-signal-green` | Qualified badge text, Run complete labels and Live indicators (27 uses as text) — the single brand hue, used only to mean "this step succeeded". Do not promote it to the primary CTA color. |
| Sprout Pulse | `#4ade80` | `--color-sprout-pulse` | Live status dots, credit counters and badge borders (14 fills, 12 text) — the luminous partner of Signal Green, sized at 6px or smaller. Never fill a surface larger than a badge with it. |
| Ember Alert | `#f87171` | `--color-ember-alert` | Not-qualified badges, error states and one solution-tile icon (5 fills) — the only negative status, and it appears exclusively inside product mockups. |

## Tokens — Typography

### Inter — the single voice for display, UI and body, run as a variable font at in-between weights · `--font-inter`

- **Substitute:** Inter (Google Fonts variable) at 400, which is the same face. Inter Tight at 400 for display sizes, where it matches the -0.02em tracked rhythm. Geist at 400, which draws a hair lighter, so set it at 420 for body to match the stroke. Inter renders true to its nominal weight, so match the numbers directly.
- **Weights:** 300, 400, 420, 440, 450, 480, 500, 580, 600
- **Sizes:** 10px, 12px, 13px, 14px, 16px, 20px, 52px, 64px
- **Line height:** 0.94, 1.0, 1.2, 1.3, 1.375, 1.43, 1.5, 1.54
- **Letter spacing:** -1.28px at 64px, -1.04px at 52px, -0.32px at 14px and 16px, -0.2px at 20px subheading, 0 at 10px, 12px, 13px and 20px heading-sm
- **OpenType features:** `"ss01"`, `"ss03"`
- **Role:** Weight 400 at 64px is the signature, and it is anti-convention against the 600 to 700 SaaS default: headlines are large and deliberately quiet, with emphasis delegated to opacity. The body sizes step on a Minor Second (13, 14, 16), then the scale jumps 2.6× from 20px straight to 52px with no h2-tier between. The result is bimodal, either reading copy or a poster, never a mid-size marketing heading. The variable weights 420, 440 and 450 are tuned so 13px to 16px text holds stroke density on a dark ground without looking bold. The ss01 and ss03 alternates give Inter its open digits and rounder forms.

### Geist Mono — technical labels for counters, IDs and workflow metadata · `--font-geist-mono`

- **Substitute:** Geist Mono (open source, OFL) at 500. JetBrains Mono at 500, which draws marginally wider, so tighten by -0.2px. IBM Plex Mono at 500, which matches stroke weight with slightly squarer terminals.
- **Weights:** 500
- **Sizes:** 14px
- **Line height:** 1.29
- **Letter spacing:** 0 at 14px
- **Role:** Mono appears 31 times, always at 14px and 500, as a single fixed register for machine-voiced data such as calendar dates, step counts and identifiers. Holding it at 500 while Inter display sits at 400 inverts the usual pairing. The machine voice is slightly heavier than the human headline, which casts the product as the confident party.

### system-ui — glyph fallback at a single size · `--font-system-ui`

- **Substitute:** Inter at 500, SF Pro Text at 500
- **Weights:** 500
- **Sizes:** 20px
- **Line height:** 1.2
- **Letter spacing:** 0 at 20px
- **Role:** detected in extracted data but not described

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | Inter | 500 | 10px | 1.2 | 0px | `--text-small` |
| caption | Inter | 500 | 12px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | Inter | 450 | 13px | 1.54 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | Inter | 400 | 14px | 1.43 | -0.32px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | Inter | 440 | 16px | 1.375 | -0.32px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | Inter | 400 | 20px | 1.5 | -0.2px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | Inter | 500 | 20px | 1.3 | 0px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | Inter | 400 | 52px | 1.0 | -1.04px | `--text-heading` |
| display | Inter | 400 | 64px | 0.94 | -1.28px | `--text-display` |

Sizes between 7.4px and 11.52px in the raw data (more than 200 elements) are product screenshots rendered as live DOM and scaled down by transform. They are mockup-internal and are not system tokens.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline at Inter weight 400 with -0.02em tracking (-1.28px at 64px) — the size carries authority, so the weight is free to stay quiet.
- Split display headlines into a #ffffff lead clause and a #ffffff80 trailing clause — opacity is the hierarchy device, replacing the bold-keyword convention.
- Restrict #22c55e and #4ade80 to status semantics (Live, Qualified, Run complete) at badge scale of 5px radius and 10px type — green must always mean "succeeded", which is non-negotiable.
- Build depth with the 1px white-at-8% subtle ring or the 0.5px white-at-14% inset — light-rings read as glass edges on #0b0c0e, where a black drop shadow is invisible.
- Step surfaces in single increments, #0b0c0e → #0e0f11 → #121214 → #151618 — a three-point RGB lift separates layers without a border competing with content.
- Fill bento cards with live, scaled product DOM rather than icons or illustrations — the 52px and 64px headlines make claims that the running mockup proves.
- Keep containers at 10px to 16px and reserve 9999px for chips, avatars and the announcement pill — the pill marks objects that float, the rounded rectangle marks objects that hold.

### Don't

- Don't bold the display headline to 600 or 700 — it collapses the opacity hierarchy into weight hierarchy and turns the restrained 400 instrument voice into conventional SaaS shouting.
- Don't give the primary button a #22c55e fill — the hue's meaning as a success verdict is spent the moment it becomes a marketing CTA.
- Don't add a 20px to 40px black drop shadow to resting cards — on #0b0c0e it reads as mud. The 40px blur is reserved for the xl popover alone.
- Don't introduce a 32px to 40px h2 tier between 20px and 52px — the bimodal scale is deliberate, and a mid-size heading reads as a template rather than a broadsheet.
- Don't brighten body copy to pure #ffffff — at 14px on #0b0c0e it halates. Use #ffffffe5, which accounts for 119 uses.
- Don't use #f87171 outside product mockups for warnings in the marketing chrome — a second chromatic voice in the frame breaks the one-hue budget.
- Don't round testimonial portraits or product screenshots independently with their own 12px radius — images run at 0px and are clipped by the parent card, and a double radius is never part of this system.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**

- canvas: #0b0c0e (Jet Canvas)
- card surface: #121214 (Carbon Card)
- primary text: #ffffffe5 (Paper Ink)
- secondary text: #ffffff80 (Fog Caption)
- border: #2d2d2f (Steel Border)
- status accent: #22c55e (Signal Green)
- primary action: no distinct CTA color

**Color in Data**

Charts and bars stay neutral, drawn in #ffffffe5 and #ffffff80 strokes on #121214, and #22c55e appears only as a 12% to 20% opacity tint behind a value or as a 6px solid dot marking a successful state, so green annotates data and is never the loudest fill on the page.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button: background #171717, text #ffffffe5, a 1px solid #2d2d2f border, border-radius 10px, padding 8px 12px, height 38px, font Inter at 14px weight 400 with letter-spacing -0.32px and line-height 20px, and no box-shadow. On hover, lift the background to #151618 and add the ring `0 0 0 1px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.08)`. Do not use green or any saturated fill.

2. Build the hero section on a #0b0c0e page with a 1240px max-width container and 96px top padding. On the left, an h1 in Inter at 64px weight 400, line-height 0.94 and letter-spacing -1.28px, with "The inbound" and "behind the" in #ffffff and "engine" and "best teams" in #ffffff80. On the right, bottom-aligned, a 16px Inter paragraph at weight 440 in #ffffff80, max-width 368px. Below, a logo row of eight monochrome marks at #ffffff80, with 64px gaps and 48px top margin. Then a 1248px product stage: background #0e0f11, border-radius 16px, 32px padding, a "Live" pill with a 6px #4ade80 dot and 10px Inter weight-500 label top-left, and "Run complete" in #22c55e top-right.

3. Build a Bento Feature Card: background #121214, a 1px solid #1f1f21 border, border-radius 12px, padding 32px. Top-left, an eyebrow in Inter at 13px weight 450 in #ffffff80. Below it with 6px spacing, a title in Inter at 20px weight 400, letter-spacing -0.2px, line-height 1.5, in #ffffffe5. Top-right, a 32px square arrow button with background #151618, a 1px #2d2d2f border and a 6px radius. The lower 60% of the card holds a scaled product mockup that fades to #0b0c0e at the bottom edge. Lay out two cards in the first row and three in the second, with 8px gaps.

4. Build a navigation bar: height 72px, transparent background over #0b0c0e, positioned relative (not sticky), inside a 1240px container. Left, a 30px-high wordmark in #ffffffe5. Center, links reading Use Cases, Product, Resources, Changelog and Pricing in Inter at 14px weight 400, letter-spacing -0.32px, #ffffffe5, with 32px gaps. Right, a Login button styled as the Primary Action Button. Login opens a popover with background #151618, a 10px radius, 6px padding, the inset ring `inset 0 0 0 0.5px rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.14)` and shadow `0 8px 40px 0 rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.32)`.

5. Build a Status Badge for the Qualified state: text #22c55e at Inter 10px weight 500, letter-spacing -0.11px, on a background of #22c55e at 20% opacity, with a 1px solid #4ade80 border, a 5px radius, 2px 6px padding and `backdrop-filter: blur(6px)`. For the Not Qualified state, use #f87171 text and a #f87171 border at 40% opacity on the same base. Place badges only inside product mockups.

### Primary Button — Iron Fill

**Role:** Main action in nav and forms

### Ghost Icon Button — Secondary

**Role:** Card arrows and Replay control

A square, quiet affordance. The spec is a background of #151618, glyph and label in #ffffffe5, a 1px solid #2d2d2f border, a 6px radius and a 32px square footprint (estimated), with a 12px horizontal padding and Inter at 13px weight 450 when a label such as "Replay" is attached, plus the subtle 1px white-at-8% ring. It anchors the top-right corner of every bento card and the bottom-right of the product stage. Use it wherever navigation is implied but a sentence-length button would compete with the headline.

### Navigation Bar

**Role:** Top-level wayfinding, logo to Login

A transparent, non-sticky strip. The spec is 72px tall with no background over #0b0c0e, a 30px-high wordmark in #ffffffe5 on the left and centered links (Use Cases, Product, Resources, Changelog, Pricing) in Inter at 14px, weight 400, -0.32px, #ffffffe5, spaced 32px apart. The right side holds a 10px-radius Login button with 8px 12px padding. The bar scrolls away with the page instead of following convention, which tells the visitor the product stage below matters more than persistent chrome.

### Announcement Pill — System Outlier

**Role:** Changelog promotion over the nav

The only light object. ## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Set every headline at Inter weight 400 with -0.02em tracking (-1.28px at 64px) — the size carries authority, so the weight is free to stay quiet.
- Split display headlines into a #ffffff lead clause and a #ffffff80 trailing clause — opacity is the hierarchy device, replacing the bold-keyword convention.
- Restrict #22c55e and #4ade80 to status semantics (Live, Qualified, Run complete) at badge scale of 5px radius and 10px type — green must always mean "succeeded", which is non-negotiable.
- Build depth with the 1px white-at-8% subtle ring or the 0.5px white-at-14% inset — light-rings read as glass edges on #0b0c0e, where a black drop shadow is invisible.
- Step surfaces in single increments, #0b0c0e → #0e0f11 → #121214 → #151618 — a three-point RGB lift separates layers without a border competing with content.
- Fill bento cards with live, scaled product DOM rather than icons or illustrations — the 52px and 64px headlines make claims that the running mockup proves.
- Keep containers at 10px to 16px and reserve 9999px for chips, avatars and the announcement pill — the pill marks objects that float, the rounded rectangle marks objects that hold.

### Don't

- Don't bold the display headline to 600 or 700 — it collapses the opacity hierarchy into weight hierarchy and turns the restrained 400 instrument voice into conventional SaaS shouting.
- Don't give the primary button a #22c55e fill — the hue's meaning as a success verdict is spent the moment it becomes a marketing CTA.
- Don't add a 20px to 40px black drop shadow to resting cards — on #0b0c0e it reads as mud. The 40px blur is reserved for the xl popover alone.
- Don't introduce a 32px to 40px h2 tier between 20px and 52px — the bimodal scale is deliberate, and a mid-size heading reads as a template rather than a broadsheet.
- Don't brighten body copy to pure #ffffff — at 14px on #0b0c0e it halates. Use #ffffffe5, which accounts for 119 uses.
- Don't use #f87171 outside product mockups for warnings in the marketing chrome — a second chromatic voice in the frame breaks the one-hue budget.
- Don't round testimonial portraits or product screenshots independently with their own 12px radius — images run at 0px and are clipped by the parent card, and a double radius is never part of this system.

## Imagery

The page uses no illustration and almost no photography. Its imagery is live product DOM: workflow node graphs, a demo-request form, an enrichment profile, a scheduling calendar and a lead-router, each rendered at roughly 55% scale inside bento cards and the 1248px product stage. Mockups sit on #0e0f11 or #121214 behind a 16px or 12px parent radius and fade to canvas at their lower edge, with no outer frame. The only photographs are grayscale customer portraits in testimonial cards, set at a 0px radius and clipped by the card, plus 24px round avatars. Icons are monochrome line glyphs in #ffffffe5, except the 20px solution-tile squares, whose blues and violets are decorative and not system tokens. There are no gradient orbs or glows. A soft vertical vignette behind the hero is decorative only. The narrative is a control room watching the pipeline run itself.

## Layout

Content holds a 1240px max-width centered on a 1920px canvas, with 96px section gaps (64–128px observed). The nav is 72px, transparent and non-sticky, with the wordmark left, five links centered and Login right. The hero sets a two-line 64px display headline left-aligned, a 16px Fog Caption paragraph bottom-aligned on the right, a monochrome logo marquee of eight marks, then the full-width 16px-radius product stage. The next section centers a 12px eyebrow and a 64px two-line headline over a bento grid of 2 cards then 3 cards with 8px gutters. A 4-column, 2-row solution-tile index follows, then testimonials in alternating rows: 2 cards (photo-led plus text), 3 text cards, then 2 again. The footer opens with a 1px #1f1f21 rule, 64px top padding and a 52px heading. At 375px, drop the display to the 52px heading token, use 64px section gaps and stack every grid to one column. Density: comfortable.

## Opacity Hierarchy

Default sets hierarchy by luminance instead of weight. Display type holds at 400, and emphasis comes from a #ffffff lead clause dimming to #ffffff80 mid-sentence, a move repeated in 20px testimonial quotes. The thesis in its plainest form is that the reader's eye is guided by brightness, not stroke. It breaks the moment someone bolds a keyword to 600, colors a phrase green, or uses a third opacity step such as 70% that blurs the two-tier contrast. To extend the system, keep exactly two tiers per text block. Assign the brighter tier to the noun phrase that names the outcome ("inbound engine", "control layer") and the dimmer tier to its context. Apply the same rule to the 12px eyebrow above the heading, which lives entirely in the dim tier.

## Status-Only Color

The chromatic budget is one hue, and its meaning is fixed: green confirms success. #22c55e and #4ade80 occur only inside product mockups, as Live dots, Qualified badges, credit counters and Run complete ticks, and nowhere in the marketing frame. That restriction is non-negotiable, because it lets the page show the product working without asking for attention. The system breaks if green becomes a CTA fill, a gradient wash behind the hero, or a hover color on nav links. Extend it by adding states, not hues. A pending state uses #ffffff80 with a spinner. A failure uses #f87171 at badge scale. Any new illustrative hue, like the solution-tile icon blues, stays inside a 20px square and is documented as decorative.

## Light-Ring Depth

On a #0b0c0e canvas, black shadows have nothing to darken, so Default builds edges out of light. Resting surfaces carry a 1px white ring at 8% opacity or a 0.5px inset at 14%, and icon wells stack three rings into a recessed bezel. Real blur, of 32px and 40px at 32% black, is spent only on floating objects: node cards in the product stage and the login popover. The discipline breaks when designers add a 24px drop shadow to resting cards, or use a #2d2d2f border and a ring on the same edge, which doubles the line weight. To extend it, assign every new component one of three states: resting (ring), recessed (inset), or floating (lg or xl). Never let it hold two at once.

## Similar Brands

- **Linear** — shares the near-black canvas, the weight-400 Inter display set with negative tracking, and a hero built from live product UI. Linear permits a violet accent in the marketing frame where Default keeps the frame grayscale.
- **Vercel** — shares Geist Mono for technical labels and the light-ring hairline elevation on dark surfaces, with Vercel running sharper 6px to 8px corners against Default's 10px to 12px cards.
- **Attio** — a go-to-market category neighbor that also sells through scaled, animated product DOM in bento cards, though Attio defaults to a light canvas.
- **Clay** — the direct enrichment-waterfall competitor, useful as contrast: Clay spends a multi-hue illustrated palette where Default spends one status green.
- **Raycast** — shares the tonal-stack dark surfaces and machined, inset-ring icon containers that simulate hardware sockets.
